text:
lina_support: Heads up — HeliosRetail (dedicated) reporting repeated 429s + p95 latency spikes for ~30m. Customer says scale is churning: up/down every ~3m. They didn't change their traffic. Logs attached: https://files.redwood/helios/429s.log :grimacing:

jamie_sre: thx. Can you paste the autoscaler events for that tenant and the policy? Also need per-tenant qps and avg latency panels.

lina_support: Autoscaler events (from our infra logs) pasted below, trimmed for noise:
```
2026-02-18T15:02:11Z HeliosRetail autoscale: scale_up -> desired=8 (from 5) reason=util>0.75
2026-02-18T15:05:12Z HeliosRetail autoscale: scale_down -> desired=4 reason=util<0.4
2026-02-18T15:08:13Z HeliosRetail autoscale: scale_up -> desired=9 reason=burst
2026-02-18T15:11:14Z HeliosRetail autoscale: scale_down -> desired=5 reason=util<0.35
```
Also included request traces link: https://traces.redwood/helios/trace/xyz

miguel_infra: hmm that cadence (3m up/down) screams short cooldown + noisy short bursts. Which autoscaler type is this? SRE-managed dynamic-proportional?

lina_support: policy: dynamic-proportional, target_util=0.65, cooldown_seconds=120, window=60s, min=3, max=24.

beth_oncall: I spun up a quick curl probe hitting the tenant gateway to reproduce. Commands:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "x-tenant: heliosretail" https://api.redwood/v1/generate; sleep 0.5; done
```
Result: intermittent 429s around the same time autoscale events happened; p95 latency jumped from 220ms -> 1.8s during scale transitions.

deploybot: [deploy] ramp_smoothing_v2 applied to cluster helios-dedicated-stable by miguel_infra at 2026-02-18T15:20:05Z

jamie_sre: can you paste the prom queries for tenant qps and pod_cpu? i'll run them for the window.

beth_oncall: prom snippets:
```
# tenant QPS
sum(rate(redwood_http_requests_total{tenant="HeliosRetail"}[1m]))
# pod count
max(kube_deployment_status_replicas{deployment="helios-tenant-HeliosRetail"})
# avg cpu
avg(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{pod=~"helios-.*HeliosRetail.*"}[1m]))
```
Outputs: qps spikes every ~3m (burst to 120r/s for ~20s), baseline ~20r/s. Pod CPU doesn't track burst well — pods saturated briefly then autoscaler fires.

miguel_infra: confirms: looking at grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/helios/tenants?from=now-1h&to=now screenshot attached. Pattern: short, high-amplitude bursts causing immediate scale_up, but cooldown too short so scale_down triggers before new pods warm up -> request queueing -> 429s. Also the KV cache warmup causes a hit to latency.

jamie_sre: proposed mitigation:
- increase cooldown_seconds from 120 -> 300
- increase window to 120s smoothing
- change target_util from 0.65 -> 0.72 so we scale slightly more conservatively up-front (fewer oscillations)
- enable burst_smoothing: true with burst_window=30s and max_burst_growth=0.25
This should reduce flip-flop for short bursts and give pods time to warm KV caches.

lina_support: will tell customer we're looking into tuning. They asked if we can do immediate rule change on their dedicated pool.

jamie_sre: we should canary on cluster helios-dedicated-canary first for 1h. If stable, roll to stable. I can do the canary now.

miguel_infra: config snippet to apply (k8s CR):
```
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: TenantAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: HeliosRetail-autoscaler
spec:
  type: dynamic-proportional
  targetUtilization: 0.72
  cooldownSeconds: 300
  smoothingWindow: 120s
  burstSmoothing:
    enabled: true
    window: 30s
    maxBurstGrowth: 0.25
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 24
```
Apply command: `kubectl apply -f helios-autoscaler-canary.yaml -n helios-dedicated-canary`

beth_oncall: I'll run the canary probe loop and watch p95 and 429 rate.

ben_custops: I'll open a support ticket to notify HeliosRetail about the plan and expected ETA (1h canary, then 1h staged rollout).

jamie_sre: action items:
- jamie_sre: apply canary and monitor for 60m (watch p95, 429 rate, pod_ready latency).
- miguel_infra: prepare rollback plan and metrics dashboard alerts for rapid rollback if 429s increase.
- beth_oncall: run synthetic probe and provide minute-by-minute snapshots.
- lina_support / ben_custops: customer comms.

lina_support: noted. Customer acknowledged and asked to prioritize — they see revenue impact.

miguel_infra: one more note: we should also check tenant-side cron jobs (batch) that may be causing the 20s bursts. ask customer for recent batch schedules. If they can't change it, we can add rate-limiter or smoothing at the ingress for that tenant.

jamie_sre: starting canary now. Will post status updates. :thumbsup:

beth_oncall: canary run started 15:26:10Z. preliminary: after applying config, first 30m show p95 down to ~300ms from 1.8s and 429s reduced by ~80%. continuing to watch.

jamie_sre: good signal. keep watchers. If stable for 60m we'll promote to stable pool and update customer.

ben_custops: ticket created: https://support.redwood/tickets/HR-429-2026-02-18. Customer notified of canary.

lina_support: thanks team — keep me posted.

jamie_sre: final note: post-mortem action item to evaluate default cooldown/window for short-burst-prone tenants and consider adaptive cooldown based on burst detection. I'll own the RFC.

beth_oncall: +1.

miguel_infra: i'll draft rollback runbook and alert thresholds (429 rate > 0.5% for 5m -> rollback).

jamie_sre: closing thread for now, will update with promotion time and metrics later.
